attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: The actual interface semantics, two-sided ownership and compatibility conditions determine whether a proposed reserve or alternate can serve that demand.
The decision horizon, separability and option-expiry conditions define what contingency the buffer portfolio must cover and for how long.
Demand and lead-time ranges plus observed actuals change which variability a proposed reserve is intended to absorb and expose fragile sizing assumptions.
Actual supplier lead times, data rights, commitments and alternatives constrain which reserve can be used and who may activate it.
The operative system, staffing, support and contingency requirements define the demand the proposed reserve must actually cover before transition.
Current recovery tests, state requirements and needed restoration time specify which reserve forms can count and disclose false substitution.
Fleet configurations, expected support duration and retirement decisions identify what reserves remain useful and when costly holdings may be retired.
The failure mode, urgency, commitments and applicable minima determine what protection the reserve must provide and whether a cheaper path is adequate.
